churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, API-base config and formatting are each confined to one module, so framework or API changes stay local; the weak spot is boundary typing — the generated-type pipeline is installed but unused, so component/loader refactors won't be caught by the compiler.

findings.issue: Five of six routes take `{ loaderData: any }`; no route imports the generated `./+types/<route>` types even though typegen is configured (app/tsconfig.json:8, package.json typecheck script).
findings.suggestion: Type loaders/components with `Route.LoaderArgs` / `Route.ComponentProps` from `./+types/...`, or at minimum reuse the `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof loader>>` trick from home.tsx across all routes.

findings.issue: Root ErrorBoundary renders the static "Not found" page for every thrown error (loader 500s included); 404s are instead handled by a returned `notFound` flag rendered in-component (routes/pokemon.tsx:37).
findings.suggestion: Follow the documented pattern: `throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 })` in loaders, render the route ErrorBoundary for the not-found UI, and branch on `useRouteError()`/`isRouteErrorResponse()` so real errors get their own message.

findings.issue: Server fetches have no timeout or AbortSignal; a hung upstream blocks an SSR request indefinitely (the concurrency limiter won't help once the slot is acquired).
findings.suggestion: Use `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` (or an AbortController with a timer) in getJSON so requests fail fast and the ErrorBoundary can render.

findings.issue: Loader serializes hidden-ability info into a `hiddenBySpecies` object keyed by id-string, which the component then rebuilds into a Map (ability.tsx:45).
findings.suggestion: Return `hidden: boolean` on each pokemon entry (as the loader already computes per species) and drop the object→Map round-trip.

findings.issue: Magic divisor 1530 for the total stat bar duplicates the (6*255) stat assumption in the markup.
findings.suggestion: Compute `stats.length * 255` (or derive the max total) next to the stats data in the loader instead of hardcoding it.

findings.issue: Regex-based URL parsing (`/\/(\d+)\/?$/`) where the platform's `new URL(...).pathname` would be clearer.
findings.suggestion: Parse the record id via `new URL(url).pathname` segments; keeps behavior obvious if API URL shapes ever change.

summary: A lean, current-generation React Router 8 app: component-prop data loading, Layout root, data() responses, a single well-bounded data-access module, and exactly the framework's recommended dependency set. The main forward-looking weakness is that it opts out of generated route types — `loaderData: any` on five of six routes means the compiler won't catch drift between loaders and components as the app or framework evolves. Error handling also bypasses the documented throw/ErrorBoundary flow, leaving 500s indistinguishable from 404s.

apis.replacement: should be imported as Route.LoaderArgs / Route.ComponentProps per the framework-mode guidance
